$schema-note: The machine-readable register of every semantic (surface, foreground) pair in the tier-2
role layer, and the contrast each pair is required to hold. It is DATA, consumed by three
gates, and it is the reason a new surface cannot ship without its contrast assertion:
every pair in the BUILT app, and also proves each
role generates a real Tailwind utility.
frontend/tests/e2e/rebrand-drill.spec.ts  re-measures every pair with tier 1 swapped to
tests/test_content_drift.py            asserts index.css declares exactly the roles listed
here — no undeclared surface, no orphan manifest row.
Why pairs and not a flat colour list: a foreground is only legible RELATIVE to a surface, so
'muted text' has no meaning on its own. Binding them here is what stops a component choosing
its text colour independently of its background — the defect that made a field change cost a
EVERY RATIO IN THIS FILE WAS RE-MEASURED ON 2026-08-20 against the new brand's pairs. Not one
was carried forward. A ratio computed against a navy ground is not evidence about a light one,
and a carried-over number would ship sub-AA text under a green gate (T-08-61). The quoted
figures are the ones `DDH_ROLE_TABLE=1 npx playwright test contrast` prints from the built
app, so a documented ratio cannot drift from the shipped one.

AAA-body.why: The running-copy pairings. This is a reading tool and three surfaces carry body text, so they clear AAA with room. Carried over verbatim from the UI-SPEC 5.5 anchor table as a THRESHOLD; every ratio measured against it was recomputed for the 2026-08-20 brand.

graphical.why: WCAG non-text contrast: a mark that carries meaning but is not read.

non-text.why: Hairlines and dashed marks ONLY. The upper bound is the assertion: raise a hairline colour to text contrast and the hairlines it draws stop reading as hairlines. The lower bound keeps it visible.

surfaces.what: The top bar and the left rail — the app's own furniture. The brand's deep navy #00063D, which the 2026-08-20 identity PROMOTED from a shadow tint to a real section surface. The ground inverted around it; the chrome did not.

foregrounds.what: Body and label copy on the chrome. 19.21:1 — the live site's own #00063D -> #FFFFFF pairing.
Secondary copy on the chrome — inactive nav, footnotes. 8.88:1.

Decoration only: separator glyphs. 3.91:1. Mixed at 42% where the light surfaces use 45%, because pure white is a brighter ink than the deep navy and 45% lands at 4.34:1 — inside the band, with almost no margin under its ceiling.
A link on the chrome is the foreground colour: the accent is not a text colour here (3.41:1).

The secondary REGISTER, dark-surface form. No longer a second hue — the brand has one — but a lightened brand blue, because #0D59F2 itself is 3.41:1 on this surface and this register carries text. 8.03:1.

The Phenome Health mark's outer arc, on the chip it sits on. 4.13:1. A brand asset, not a UI mark — it is registered here so the logo carries a contrast assertion like everything else, and so that retiring a UI accent can never restyle it again (T-08-65).
The mark's middle arc. 19.21:1.

The mark's inner arc — the brand's teal, which survives ONLY inside the mark. 8.93:1. On the accent fill this chip used to carry, the same three arcs measured 1.21 / 5.63 / 2.62, so this row is also the assertion that caught a two-thirds-invisible logo.

surfaces.what: Cards, panes, popovers, the ledger — the working surface, where the reviewer's eyes live. Pure white on the brand's pale-blue field, which is how the ledger still reads as PAPER ON A FIELD after the ground inverted. Two brand colours, not a shadow: a shadow is not a surface and does not survive print or forced-colours mode.

foregrounds.what: Body copy on a card. 21:1 — the brand puts pure black on its paper.
Secondary copy, column headers, the not-judged label. 7.09:1. Mixed from the DEEP NAVY rather than from --on-raised: black at 68% over white is a neutral grey, and this brand is one hue family.
Hairlines and dashed marks only. 3.18:1.
CDE identifiers, DOIs, outbound references. 5.63:1.

The secondary REGISTER, light-surface form: the brand's slate. 7.99:1. It carries what the retired teal carried (cohort codes, informational rules), so the step back from the primary register is now by VALUE rather than by a competing hue.
adopt / approved / judged coherent. 5.14:1.
refine / split / qualify — the coherence flag, the most important signal on Gate 1. 6.45:1.
The destructive TEXT register. 5.70:1.
The destructive FILL hue, also used as a text colour. 4.64:1 — the thinnest margin in the system by construction; never tint it further.
The informational register, folded into the action accent. 5.63:1.

The accent as a GLYPH or emphasised figure on paper — a card-title icon, an active label. 5.63:1. Same value as --link-on-raised and a different statement: a title icon is not a link, and calling it one is the lie `ph-navy` was.

surfaces.what: The page field the raised surfaces sit on. INVERTED on 2026-08-20 from the navy ground back to a light one, following the brand — #D5E0F6, which is the live site's ground BY AREA (11,356px of page height; white appears only as cards and insets inside it, so an element-COUNT reading of the same page gets it backwards). Its foregrounds were the gap that motivated this whole layer: no anchor covered text-on-field, so the field inherited the CHROME's foreground and bare copy rendered cream-on-cream while the contrast gate stayed green. The pair has now survived two ground changes in opposite directions without a component edit.

foregrounds.what: Bare copy directly on the field. 14.47:1. AAA-body, not AAA: the field carries running copy (page headers, section leads, standing notes) exactly as the chrome does, so it is held to the same 13:1 the other body surfaces are.
Secondary copy on the field — a page subtitle, a standing caveat. 6.21:1.
Hairlines and separator glyphs on the field. 3.01:1, deliberately inside the non-text band.

A link on the field IS the foreground colour, 14.47:1. The SAME decision as before the ground inverted, re-made for a completely different reason: the accent used to measure 2.47:1 on the navy ground and be invisible, and now measures 4.24:1 on the pale-blue one — a legal graphical mark, still below AA as body text. This is the one field role that is not a mechanical copy of the chrome pair.

The accent on the field as a GRAPHICAL object only — the eyebrow's filled square, a marker, a rule. 4.24:1. This role REPLACES the prohibition that used to sit here: the brand now supports the pairing for a mark and not for text, and a positive assertion at the non-text floor says that, where a `max: 3` bound would simply have started failing.

surfaces.what: Header bands, row hover, inset panels INSIDE a raised surface — the brand's palest blue. An inset sits inside a card, a field sits under one; keeping them separate is what let the field move twice without dragging every table header band with it.

foregrounds.what: Copy in a table header band or a hovered row. 18.32:1.
Secondary copy in an inset panel. 6.66:1.
A link in an inset panel. 4.91:1.

surfaces.what: The SECOND inset step: pressed, selected, a badge fill. An interaction has two states — hover is a hint, pressed is a commitment — and one step cannot say both. Collapsing the two is how a button stops acknowledging the click. It was DERIVED (the raised ink at 6%); it is now the brand's third light step outright, because the brand supplies two steps above the paper and using them says the same thing in brand colours.

foregrounds.what: Copy on a pressed control or a badge fill. 15.82:1.
Secondary copy on that fill — a toast's description line. 6.21:1.

The accent as a label on the fill. REDECLARED for this brand: the accent ITSELF measures 4.24:1 on this step and is sub-AA, where the old 6% derivation gave it 5.03:1. So the role is now a darkened accent (85% blue into the deep navy) at 5.20:1. The assertion survived; what backs it changed — which is exactly what a role layer is for.

surfaces.what: The well a coverage/verdict bar is drawn in. A bar and its track are a (surface, foreground) pair like any other, and asserting it is what pins --series-residual at 62%: it clears the graphical floor against PAPER at 5.67:1 but only 4.56:1 against the track it is actually drawn in, and the tighter of two constraints is the one that decides the value.

foregrounds.what: Probed as `text-` because the gate reads a foreground as `color`; the bar itself is painted with `bg-on-track`, which is the SAME `--color-on-track` key, so proving one proves the other. The achromatic bar itself — the residual mark, aliased so the two are one value rather than two neutrals half a step apart. 4.56:1.

surfaces.what: THE ACCENT AS A FULL-BLEED SURFACE — new on 2026-08-20. The live site fills whole sections with #0D59F2 carrying near-white copy, and the previous role set could not express that: the accent existed only as a foreground and an action fill. Declared here, with its bound foreground, so the surface arrives WITH a contrast assertion instead of implicitly (T-08-63) — the failure being pre-empted is a #0D59F2 panel added to a gate screen with no foreground pair, which is the cream-on-cream defect in a new colour. Deliberately the same VALUE as --accent and a separate ROLE: a fill that carries running copy and an action tint diverge the moment either has to move. There is no gradient here on purpose — the site's apparent blue gradient measures as two flat fills at different alphas, and the whole live document declares zero CSS gradients.

foregrounds.what: Copy on a full-bleed accent section. 5.63:1. The site's own pairing is #0D59F2 -> #EBEFFF at 4.88:1; pure white buys the margin back.

surfaces.what: The single primary action per screen. It is a SURFACE when filled, so it carries a bound foreground like any other.

foregrounds.what: The label inside a filled primary action. 5.63:1.

surfaces.what: The primary action under the pointer. A hover is a SURFACE with its own bound label, not an opacity trick — dropping the button's alpha would show the field through it.

foregrounds.what: The same label, on the hovered fill. It can only improve on the base (5.63 -> 7.54) because the fill darkens toward the paper ink.
The label on the pressed fill (10.16:1).
The label inside a filled destructive action. 4.64:1.

surfaces.what: A destructive action under the pointer.

foregrounds.what: The label on the hovered destructive fill (6.18:1). The base is the thinnest margin in the system at 4.64:1, so the hover state is where it gets room.
The label on the pressed destructive fill (8.34:1).

surfaces.what: The wash a success badge sits on.

foregrounds.what: The badge's own label. 4.62:1 — derived over the paper, so it followed the paper from cream to white without being touched.

surfaces.what: The wash the coherence flag and the site-wide caveat band sit on.

foregrounds.what: The flag's own label. 5.67:1. The one pair in the whole manifest painted end to end from product-owned status primitives, so it is also the one pair that cannot move in a rebrand — named as such in the drill's fixture.

surfaces.what: The wash a destructive status label sits on.

foregrounds.what: The label's own text. 5.20:1.

surfaces.what: The wash an informational callout sits on.

foregrounds.what: The callout's own text. 5.00:1.

graphicalMarks.note: Charts live on raised surfaces. Each step is a graphical object, so 3:1 is the floor, not 4.5:1. Every step gained margin when the paper went from warm cream to pure white; none of them was re-tuned for it, which is the wash/derivation discipline paying off.

prohibited.why: UI-SPEC 5.2, the hard rule: the accent is not a TEXT colour on the chrome. On the chrome an action is outlined in a paper-alpha rule with the chrome's own foreground. REDECLARED for the 2026-08-20 brand, not carried: the bound was 3 when the chrome was #1E2A52 and the accent measured 2.47:1; on the brand's deeper #00063D it measures 3.41:1, which is a legal graphical mark. The rule being asserted was never 'blue is invisible here' — it was 'a link on the chrome is the foreground colour' — so the bound moves to the AA line and keeps asserting the thing that is actually true. Leaving it at 3 would have failed for the right reason with the wrong number; deleting it would have let a blue label onto the chrome the first time someone tried.

UI-SPEC 5.4: the dark-surface form of the secondary register never touches the paper (2.39:1). Use --accent-2-on-raised. The relationship survived the brand replacing a second HUE with a second VALUE — it used to be a bright teal that washed out on cream, and it is now a lightened blue that washes out on white, which is the same mistake in a different palette.

The MIRROR of the pre-inversion row this replaces. While the field was navy, the prohibited pairing was the LIGHT-surface form of the secondary register on it; now the field is light, it is the DARK-surface form that is prohibited (1.80:1). The prohibition encodes a RELATIONSHIP — the wrong form of the register for the surface — and the relationship is what survives a ground inversion. Its predecessor (`--accent-2-on-raised on --surface-field`) is void: slate on the pale-blue field measures 6.02:1 and is perfectly legal now.

1.15:1, and the exact original defect this whole layer was written for. Bare copy inherited the CHROME's foreground and rendered cream-on-cream on the paper while every declared pair measured fine. It replaces `--on-raised on --surface-field`, which measured 1.04:1 while the field was navy and measures 15.82:1 now that it is light — void as a number, so it is re-asserted as the pairing that is STILL wrong. An unmigrated component that keeps `text-on-chrome` inside a card lands here.

1:1 — the field's foreground on the chrome, which after the ground inversion resolve to the same primitive. The other direction of the row above, and the one a component picks up by drifting out of `<main>` into the rail. Two prohibitions rather than one because the two subtrees fail independently: a card that keeps the chrome's ink, and a rail item that keeps the field's.
